behavior.arguments: rdi = a holder whose [rdi+0x68] points to a struct whose +0x108 field is the mark value; rsi = a table struct with +0x00 (additive count), +0x48 (first-array pointer), +0x50 (second-array begin), +0x58 (second-array end).
behavior.count_rule: N = [rsi] + (([rsi+0x58] - [rsi+0x50]) >> 3), arithmetic shift. N == 0 returns immediately with no writes; otherwise the outer loop runs while i != N, i starting at 0 and incrementing by 1.

edges.empty_head: entry whose [entry+0x8f8] head points to itself ([head] == head) -> no writes for that entry.
edges.entry_boundary: entry 7 reads from the [rsi+0x48] array, entry 8 reads from the [rsi+0x50] array; a 9-entry walk with count 8 + 1 marks the 9th entry's chain.
edges.mask_node_marked: node with [node+0xcc8] == 0x00ffffffffffffff is overwritten with the mark value and the walk continues.
edges.non_mask_node_stops: node with [node+0xcc8] != 0x00ffffffffffffff is left untouched and the walk stops for that entry.
edges.self_loop_link: a link whose +0x00 points to itself marks its mask node once, then stops on the revisit because the field no longer equals the mask.

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with endbr64; 38 instructions, 7 branches, no calls: mark = [[rdi+0x68]+0x108]; N computed; loop over entries (first 8 from the [rsi+0x48] array, rest from the [rsi+0x50] array); per entry, head = [entry+0x8f8], cur = [head]; if cur == head, next entry; else while [node+0xcc8] == mask (node = [cur+0x10]): cur = [cur], [node+0xcc8] = mark, stop if cur == head.
behavior.mark_rule: mark = [[rdi+0x68]+0x108], computed once before the loop and never changed inside it. Every mark write stores exactly this value into [node+0xcc8].
behavior.return_rule: No return-value contract is claimed: ret leaves rax holding the last walk value, which varies by path.
behavior.walk_rule: Per entry: rcx = [entry+0x8f8]; cur = [rcx]; if cur == rcx, entry done with no writes. Else repeat: node = [cur+0x10]; if [node+0xcc8] != 0x00ffffffffffffff, entry done (node untouched); else cur = [cur], [node+0xcc8] = mark, and if cur == rcx, entry done.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; four sites found, each confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from its caller FDE start. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan. No caller purpose is claimed.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: No R_X86_64_RELATIVE (or any other type) record in any .rela.* section names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries).

reverification.method: The window bytes were decoded with Capstone and executed by a small interpreter (deriving every operand from the decode, so it is independent of the rule's transcription) over synthetic layouts: count sweeps, entry-boundary cases, empty heads, mask/non-mask chains, and self-loop links. The interpreter is not committed (needs Capstone, not stdlib).
